s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal mass with chronic vomiting and right upper-quadrant pain
salient_findings: Large, firm, palpable mass in the right upper quadrant
Large retroperitoneal mass with fatty and soft-tissue components
key_facts: 2-year history of intermittent vomiting
Right upper-quadrant pain
Sensation of fullness on the right side of the abdomen
Denies urinary symptoms or changes in bowel habits
History of heavy menstruation and iron deficiency anemia
Oral iron therapy for over 10 years
Beta-thalassemia trait on hemoglobin electrophoresis
Hemoglobin levels ranging from 6 to 10 g/dL
Abdominal ultrasonography showed a well-defined hyperechoic heterogeneous mass
Contrast-enhanced CT showed a well-defined, encapsulated retroperitoneal lesion
MRI confirmed a large right retroperitoneal predominantly fatty mass

differentials: Paraganglioma of the organ of Zuckerkandl
Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor with rhabdomyosarcomatous differentiation
per_call: Paraganglioma of the organ of Zuckerkandl
Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor with rhabdomyosarcomatous differentiation

shortlist.label: Myelolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large, firm, palpable mass with a rounded surface and ill-defined borders, and imaging showing a well-defined, encapsulated retroperitoneal lesion of mostly fat density

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging showing a large right retroperitoneal predominantly fatty mass, which is consistent with a lipoma

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging showing a large right retroperitoneal mass with areas of soft-tissue density, which could be indicative of a liposarcoma

shortlist.label: Adrenal myelolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Location of the mass in the hepatorenal space, which is consistent with an adrenal myelolipoma

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging showing a well-defined, encapsulated retroperitoneal lesion with internal areas of soft-tissue density, which could be indicative of a teratoma

raw.rationale: The presence of a large, well-defined, encapsulated retroperitoneal lesion with mostly fat density and internal areas of soft-tissue density, along with the patient's beta-thalassemia trait and history of anemia, supports the diagnosis of adrenal myelolipoma, a rare benign tumor composed of adipose tissue and hematopoietic elements.

rejected.label: Myelolipoma
rejected.why: Too general, as myelolipoma can occur in various locations, whereas adrenal myelolipoma specifically matches the tumor's location and characteristics.

rejected.label: Retroperitoneal lipoma
rejected.why: Does not account for the soft-tissue components and hematopoietic elements within the tumor.

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: Typically exhibits more aggressive features, such as invasion of adjacent organs, which is not evident in this case.

rejected.label: Retroperitoneal teratoma
rejected.why: Usually contains multiple tissue types, including epithelial, muscular, and neural elements, which are not described in the imaging findings.
